newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ruling party to pick mayor candidate today.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ruling party to pick mayor candidate today.

text.p: Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) was to pick Wednesday night its candidate for the year's most closely watched election -- that of the first elected mayor of Mexico City.
The PRI, which is trailing both main opposition parties in the capital according to some polls, will be the first party to choose its candidate.

In a break from tradition, three politicians are openly competing for the nomination and the result will be decided by a secret ballot of some 200 delegates from the PRI's Mexico City Political Council.
Polls indicate that Alfredo del Mazo, an old-guard politician who currently runs the federal housing scheme Infonavit, is the favorite of voters but the party's choice is less certain.

Close aides say President Ernesto Zedillo will break with long-established practice by allowing delegates a free vote and not indicating a preferred candidate. However, political analysts are more skeptical, saying men close to the president have been lobbying on behalf of Jose Antonio Gonzalez Fernandez, the Mexico City chief prosecutor.
The third candidate is Manuel Jimenez Guzman, a little known politician from the Mexico City legislative assembly who is popular with the party's local grass roots.

Whoever wins the nomination faces an uphill struggle to win the July mayor's election. Polls put the conservative National Action Party (PAN) way ahead of the PRI among voters. The PAN will choose its candidate in a special convention March 2.
The Mexico City mayor has hitherto been handpicked by the president of the republic, and has always been a PRI man.
